why / where it would go: It is the first statement of the per-series lambda and writes element 0 of the WHOLE output, from every one of batch_size threads. # theirs: cuBLAS getrf / getri / gemm themselves
why / where it would go: Closed calls with no MAX equivalent for a batched LU. Their association order and their pivot tie rule are not readable from source, so the spelling here is chosen and written down rather than inherited: pivot = FIRST index of the strictly largest magnitude in the column (a strict `>` scan, so no signed zero can displace the other), row swap, L column = a / pivot, trailing update fma(-l, u, a), then the inverse column by column by permuted forward and backward substitution, serial ascending. That the tie rule is OURS and not theirs is exactly why sabotage (e) in SABOTAGES.md perturbs it

# theirs: cuml python/cuml/cuml/tsa/batched_lbfgs.py: batched_fmin_lbfgs_b and its scipy.optimize._lbfgsb.setulb state machine
why / where it would go: cuML has no L-BFGS of its own here; it drives scipy's Fortran L-BFGS-B once per series in float64, with bounds=None so the box constraints are inert. scipy is NOT taken as a runtime dependency: the wheel depends on numpy alone, and a third-party host float64 optimizer in the middle of a certified path would put the fitted coefficients outside anything this repository can reproduce. The SHAPE is kept (host state machine per series, ONE batched device evaluation per candidate point) and the ALGORITHM is cuML's OWN L-BFGS, already ported in glm/impl/glm/qn/, re-spelled per series in arima/impl/arima/lbfgs_host.mojo. THIS MEANS THE ITERATE SEQUENCE IS NOT cuML's: scipy's More-Thuente line search, history update and stopping constants all differ from cuML's backtracking Armijo. What is claimed is a converged ML fit reproducible bit for bit across vendors; what is NOT claimed is agreement with cuML's iterates or its iteration count

# theirs: cuBLAS gelsBatched itself
why / where it would go: A closed call with no MAX equivalent for a batched least squares. Ours is a Householder QR with back substitution, one thread per series, serial ascending through identical_mul_add, with the reflector sign, the fold order and a diagonal rank test all CHOSEN and written down (arima/impl/linalg/batched/least_squares.mojo, arima/SEAMS.tsv). The normal-equations route this tree already owns (cholesky/potrf_lower, glm lstsq_eig) was assessed and REJECTED on accuracy: forming A'A squares the condition number, and a lag matrix from a near-unit-root series is exactly where Float32 cannot afford that. check_qr_beats_normal_equations_on_ill_conditioning measures it rather than arguing it. THROUGHPUT DEVIATION: theirs parallelizes inside each problem, ours is serial in the row count, which is nothing at the shipped shapes and visible at n_obs in the tens of thousands
